answers.answer: The minimum setup to create and run a basic LlmAgent using @google/adk requires: 1) Install the package via npm: `npm install @google/adk`, 2) Set the API key environment variable GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY, 3) Import LlmAgent and InMemoryRunner from @google/adk, 4) Create an LlmAgent with a name and model, 5) Create an InMemoryRunner with the agent, 6) Call runner.runAsync() with userId, sessionId, and newMessage. Example: `const agent = new LlmAgent({name: 'my_agent', model: 'gemini-2.5-flash'}); const runner = new InMemoryRunner({agent}); const session = await runner.sessionService.getOrCreateSession({appName: runner.appName, userId: 'user1', sessionId: 'session1'}); for await (const event of runner.runAsync({userId: 'user1', sessionId: session.id, newMessage: {role: 'user', parts: [{text: 'Hello'}]}})) { console.log(event); }`

ADK-JS supports the following environment variables: 1) GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY - API key for Gemini API authentication, 2) GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT - GCP project ID for Vertex AI mode, 3) GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION - GCP region for Vertex AI (e.g., 'us-central1'), 4) GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI - boolean flag to switch from Gemini API to Vertex AI mode, 5) ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS - controls whether request/response content is included in OpenTelemetry traces (defaults to 'true', set to 'false' or '0' to disable).

adk-js is a monorepo with two npm workspaces: 1) core (@google/adk) - The main package containing the Agent Development Kit core functionality, located in the 'core' directory, 2) dev (@google/adk-devtools) - Development tools package in the 'dev' directory, providing the CLI tool. The root package.json defines workspaces: ['core', 'dev'].

The key runtime dependencies of @google/adk are: 1) @google/genai (^1.37.0) - Official Google Generative AI SDK, 2) @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (^1.26.0) - Model Context Protocol SDK for MCP tool integration, 3) google-auth-library (^10.3.0) - Google authentication library for Vertex AI, 4) zod (^4.2.1) - Schema validation library, 5) lodash-es (^4.17.23) - Utility library for deep cloning, 6) zod-to-json-schema (^3.25.1) - Converts Zod schemas to JSON Schema format.

To configure ADK-JS to use Vertex AI instead of the Gemini API: 1) Set the GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI environment variable to 'true' or '1', 2) Set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT to your GCP project ID, 3) Set GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION to your GCP region (e.g., 'us-central1'), 4) Ensure Application Default Credentials (ADC) are configured. The GoogleLLMVariant enum distinguishes between GEMINI_API and VERTEX_AI modes.

The public exports from @google/adk are defined in two entry points: 1) common.ts - Contains all the core browser-compatible exports (~140 items), 2) index.ts - Main entry point that re-exports everything from common.ts plus Node.js-specific exports. 3) index_web.ts - Browser entry point that only exports from common.ts. The dual ESM/CJS build is configured via build.js using esbuild.

ADK-JS supports browser environments via the index_web.ts entry point. The browser build only exports from common.ts, excluding Node.js-specific capabilities like GcsArtifactService, telemetry exports, and MCP tools. The browser bundle still includes core functionality: all agent types, InMemoryRunner with in-memory services, FunctionTool and AgentTool, Gemini model (API key mode only), and BasePlugin.

ADK-JS requires TypeScript version ^5.9.2. The compiler settings in tsconfig.json extend from gts (Google TypeScript Style) with: target: ES2020, module: nodenext, lib: ['ES2022', 'DOM'], moduleResolution: nodenext, esModuleInterop: true, skipLibCheck: true. The ES2020 target ensures modern JavaScript features are available.

The agent hierarchy is structured with BaseAgent as the abstract root class. Concrete implementations extend BaseAgent: 1) LlmAgent - Agent powered by language models, 2) LoopAgent - Runs sub-agents in a loop until maxIterations or escalate, 3) SequentialAgent - Runs sub-agents sequentially (LoopAgent with maxIterations=1), 4) ParallelAgent - Runs sub-agents concurrently with isolated branches. All agents use Symbol-based type checking instead of instanceof.

ADK-JS uses a Symbol-based type guard pattern for runtime type checking. Each class defines a unique Symbol via Symbol.for() with a namespaced key. This pattern was chosen over instanceof because Symbol.for() creates global symbols that work across different module instances and bundler boundaries. Symbols survive serialization/deserialization better than prototype chains and work correctly with duck typing patterns.

The complete request processing pipeline in LlmAgent consists of request processors executed in order: 1) BasicLlmRequestProcessor, 2) IdentityLlmRequestProcessor, 3) InstructionsLlmRequestProcessor, 4) ContentRequestProcessor, 5) RequestConfirmationLlmRequestProcessor, 6) CodeExecutionRequestProcessor, 7) AgentTransferLlmRequestProcessor. These run sequentially via generators before the LLM call.

InvocationContext serves as the central context object for an agent invocation, carrying all necessary references and state. It contains: 1) Service references (artifactService, sessionService, memoryService, credentialService), 2) Current execution state (invocationId, agent, session, userContent, branch), 3) Runtime configuration (runConfig, pluginManager), 4) InvocationCostManager that tracks numberOfLlmCalls and enforces maxLlmCalls limit.

The context hierarchy consists of three layers: 1) ReadonlyContext - Base layer providing read-only access, 2) CallbackContext extends ReadonlyContext - Adds mutable state and artifact operations, 3) ToolContext extends CallbackContext - Adds tool-specific capabilities like requestCredential() and searchMemory(). This ensures progressive capability enhancement.

AsyncGenerator is used throughout ADK-JS for streaming execution patterns: 1) Agent execution: BaseAgent.runAsync() returns AsyncGenerator<Event>, 2) LLM streaming: BaseLlm.generateContentAsync() returns AsyncGenerator<LlmResponse>, 3) Request/Response processors: BaseLlmRequestProcessor.runAsync() are AsyncGenerators, 4) Tool execution pipeline: handleFunctionCallsAsync yields events. For-await-of loops compose generators. Benefits: Memory efficient streaming, backpressure support, composable pipelines, cancellation via generator.return().

ADK-JS uses several design patterns: 1) Template Method: BaseAgent.runAsync() defines execution skeleton with runAsyncImpl() as abstract method, 2) Strategy: BaseLlm interface allows swapping implementations, 3) Registry/Factory: LLMRegistry maintains model name patterns to BaseLlm mappings, 4) Observer/Hook: BasePlugin defines lifecycle hooks, 5) Chain of Responsibility: Request/response processors run sequentially, 6) Decorator: Processors wrap LLM calls with pre/post-processing, 7) Builder: createRunConfig(), createEvent() use builder pattern.

The delta/event-sourcing pattern works through State and EventActions: 1) State class maintains value (current committed state) and delta (pending changes), 2) EventActions tracks changes per event: stateDelta, artifactDelta, transferToAgent, escalate, requestedAuthConfigs, requestedToolConfirmations, 3) Event sourcing flow: CallbackContext wraps State with eventActions.stateDelta, events carry stateDelta to session, BaseSessionService.appendEvent() applies stateDelta. Benefits: Atomic state updates per event, rollback capability, artifact versioning.

LlmAgentConfig extends BaseAgentConfig with: 1) model (string | BaseLlm) - LLM to use, 2) instruction (string | InstructionProvider) - Agent behavior guidance, 3) tools (ToolUnion[]) - Array of tools, 4) generateContentConfig (GenerateContentConfig) - Model parameters, 5) disallowTransferToParent/disallowTransferToPeers (boolean), 6) includeContents ('default' | 'none') - Controls conversation history, 7) inputSchema/outputSchema (Schema), 8) outputKey (string), 9) beforeModelCallback/afterModelCallback, 10) requestProcessors/responseProcessors, 11) codeExecutor (BaseCodeExecutor).

Agent transfer works via the built-in transfer_to_agent FunctionTool. The transfer mechanism: 1) Tool definition: FunctionTool with name 'transfer_to_agent', parameter agentName, 2) Transfer target determination: getTransferTargets() returns available agents based on disallow flags, 3) Execution: transferToAgent() validates target and sets event.actions.transferToAgent, 4) Routing: Runner.determineAgentForResumption() uses this to find the next agent. DisallowTransferToParent flag also prevents replying to end-user.

LoopAgent runs sub-agents sequentially in a loop until maxIterations is reached or an escalate action occurs. Configuration: maxIterations (number, default Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). Behavior: For each iteration < maxIterations, runs each sub-agent in sequence, checks event.actions.escalate - if true, exits immediately. The escalate pattern allows sub-agents to signal early termination.

ParallelAgent implements concurrent sub-agent execution using branch isolation and Promise.race-based merging. Implementation: 1) Branch creation: createBranchCtxForSubAgent() creates isolated InvocationContext, 2) Concurrent execution: Maps each sub-agent to subAgent.runAsync(branchContext), 3) Event merging: mergeAgentRuns() uses Promise.race pattern to yield events from whichever generator produces next. This enables multiple agents to work concurrently while maintaining event ordering per agent.

Agent naming rules enforced by validateAgentName(): 1) Must be a valid identifier: Starts with letter or underscore, contains letters, digits, underscores, hyphens. Validated via regex: /^[\p{ID_Start}$_][\p{ID_Continue}$_-]*$/u, 2) Cannot be 'user': Reserved for end-user input. Validation happens in BaseAgent constructor before setting this.name.

beforeAgentCallback and afterAgentCallback provide hooks into agent execution lifecycle: 1) Signature: SingleAgentCallback = (context: CallbackContext) => Promise<Content | undefined>, 2) beforeAgentCallback: Runs before runAsyncImpl(), early-exit semantics if returns Content, 3) afterAgentCallback: Runs after runAsyncImpl(), replaces response if returns Content, 4) Array behavior: Callbacks execute in order until one returns non-undefined value. Execution order: Plugin callbacks first, then agent callbacks.

The instruction system supports multiple formats: 1) String instructions with template syntax: Use {key} to inject session state values. Supports optional keys with '?' suffix: {key?}. Supports prefixes: {app:key}, {user:key}, {temp:key}. Can inject artifacts: {artifact.filename}, 2) InstructionProvider functions: (context: ReadonlyContext) => string | Promise<string>. Receives ReadonlyContext with session access, 3) instruction vs globalInstruction: instruction applies to specific agent, globalInstruction applies to entire tree (only root's used).

The outputKey configuration stores agent output in session state: 1) Configuration: outputKey (string) - State key where output stored, outputSchema (Schema) - Optional JSON schema, 2) Saving logic: maybeSaveOutputToState() checks outputKey, waits for final response, extracts text. If outputSchema set, parses as JSON. Stores in event.actions.stateDelta[outputKey], 3) State persistence: Statedelta applied to session.state by BaseSessionService.appendEvent(), 4) Usage: Tools and callbacks can access via state.get(outputKey). When outputSchema set, tools/transfers disabled.

Model inheritance allows child agents to inherit the LLM from ancestor agents via the canonicalModel getter. Inheritance logic: 1) Check if this.model is BaseLlm instance - return it, 2) Check if this.model is non-empty string - call LLMRegistry.newLlm(this.model), 3) Traverse parent chain - set ancestorAgent = this.parentAgent, while ancestorAgent exists, check if LlmAgent and return ancestorModel, 4) If no model found - throw error. LLMRegistry.newLlm() uses LRU cache to avoid duplicate instances.

The includeContents option controls what conversation history is sent to the model: 1) Configuration: includeContents?: 'default' | 'none' (defaults to 'default'), 2) Processing: If 'default' - calls getContents() for full history, If 'none' - calls getCurrentTurnContents() for current turn only. 3) Use cases: 'default' for multi-turn dialogue with state tracking, 'none' for stateless operations, single-shot tasks, privacy/context isolation. This affects token usage and model context window utilization significantly.

To create a FunctionTool with typed parameters using Zod schemas, use the ToolOptions interface which accepts Zod v3 and v4 schemas. The FunctionTool constructor takes name (optional, auto-derived), description (required), parameters (optional, can be ZodObject, Schema, or undefined), execute (function to run), isLongRunning (optional boolean). When parameters is ZodObject, validates input using schema.parse() before execution.

AgentTool wraps an agent as a tool. It takes AgentToolConfig with agent (BaseAgent reference) and skipSummarization (optional boolean). When executed, creates temporary Runner with ForwardingArtifactService that forwards artifact operations to parent's ToolContext. Creates temp session with parent's state, runs sub-agent with user's message, forwards stateDelta updates back to parent. The skipSummarization option prevents model from summarizing output.

MCPToolset and MCPTool provide integration with Model Context Protocol servers. MCPToolset takes MCPConnectionParams (StdioConnectionParams or StreamableHTTPConnectionParams) and optional ToolPredicate/string[] filter. MCPSessionManager manages MCP client sessions using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. MCPToolset.getTools() calls session.listTools() and wraps each in MCPTool instance. MCPTool translates MCP tool schemas to Gemini format. When executed, creates session and sends callTool request.

GoogleSearchTool is a built-in tool for Gemini models that retrieves search results. Unlike FunctionTool, its processLlmRequest() adds Tool config object directly to llmRequest.config.tools. For Gemini 1.x models, it adds {googleSearchRetrieval: {}} and throws error if other tools present. For Gemini 2+ models, it adds {googleSearch: {}}. Since this is server-side built-in tool, runAsync() returns Promise.resolve() without local execution.

ToolContext extends CallbackContext and provides tools with: 1) Session state access via inherited state property, 2) Artifact operations: loadArtifact(filename, version?), saveArtifact(filename, artifact), listArtifacts(), 3) Memory search via searchMemory(query), 4) Credential requests via requestCredential(authConfig) and getAuthResponse(authConfig), 5) Tool confirmation via requestConfirmation({hint?, payload?}). Also exposes functionCallId (maps responses to calls) and actions property (alias for eventActions).

beforeToolCallback and afterToolCallback intercept tool execution. Execution flow: 1) Plugin beforeToolCallback runs first, if returns non-null, that becomes response and callbacks skip, 2) If plugins don't override, canonical beforeToolCallbacks array iterated, 3) If no override, tool.runAsync() called, 4) After execution, plugin afterToolCallback runs, 5) If plugins don't override, canonical afterToolCallbacks iterated. Key pattern: any non-null return short-circuits rest of chain. Plugins always run before canonical callbacks.

BaseToolset is abstract class enabling dynamic tool discovery and filtering. It has constructor accepting toolFilter (ToolPredicate function or string array). ToolPredicate is function: (tool: BaseTool, readonlyContext: ReadonlyContext) => boolean. Abstract getTools(context?: ReadonlyContext) method returns Promise<BaseTool[]>. Protected isToolSelected(tool, context) applies filter. BaseToolset differs from BaseTool - BaseTool is single concrete tool with runAsync(), BaseToolset is collection with dynamic discovery.

Long-running tools are tools that may take time to complete and return asynchronously. Mechanism: 1) BaseTool has isLongRunning boolean property (default false), 2) LongRunningFunctionTool extends FunctionTool, automatically sets isLongRunning: true, appends note to description, 3) During function call handling, if tool.isLongRunning and response null, loop continues without creating response event, 4) Function call IDs tracked in longRunningToolIds Set, 5) Events can have longRunningToolIds array field listing IDs of long-running calls.

Tool confirmation allows tools to request user confirmation before execution. Mechanism: 1) ToolContext.requestConfirmation({hint?, payload?}) creates ToolConfirmation with hint, confirmed (initially false), payload, 2) Stored in eventActions.requestedToolConfirmations[functionCallId], 3) After tools execute, generateRequestConfirmationEvent() checks and creates special function call with name 'adk_request_confirmation', args containing originalFunctionCall and toolConfirmation, 4) RequestConfirmationLlmRequestProcessor handles confirmation round-trip, prompts user, when confirmed, resumes original tool execution.

The pauseOnToolCalls option in RunConfig enables client-side tool execution by allowing agent loop to suspend on ANY tool call. When set to true (default false), agent execution pauses whenever tools about to be called, yielding control to client. Client can inspect tool calls, decide execution, modify arguments, execute tools client-side, provide results back to resume agent. This is distinct from long-running tools, provides general mechanism for client to control all tool execution.

BaseLlm is abstract class defining LLM contract. It has constructor taking {model: string}. Core method is generateContentAsync(llmRequest: LlmRequest, stream?: boolean): AsyncGenerator<LlmResponse, void>. When stream=true, yields multiple partial responses; when false, yields single complete response. The connect(llmRequest: LlmRequest): Promise<BaseLlmConnection> method creates live bidirectional connection. maybeAppendUserContent(llmRequest) ensures LLM can continue by appending user message if needed. Has static supportedModels property (array of string/RegExp patterns) for registry.

The Gemini class implements BaseLlm for Google's Gemini models. Constructor takes GeminiParams: model (defaults to 'gemini-2.5-flash'), apiKey, vertexai (boolean), project, location, headers. Initialization checks GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI env var; for Vertex AI requires project/location; for API key mode reads GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY. The apiClient getter lazily creates GoogleGenAI instances. The apiBackend getter returns VERTEX_AI or GEMINI_API based on apiClient.vertexai. generateContentAsync() implements both streaming and non-streaming. The connect() method creates live connection.

LLMRegistry is factory/registry pattern mapping model names to BaseLlm implementations. It has static llmRegistryDict: Map<string | RegExp, BaseLlmType> storing regex patterns to LLM classes. Static register<T extends BaseLlm>(llmCls) iterates supportedModels and registers each pattern. resolve(model: string) searches llmRegistryDict entries, creating anchored RegExp, tests if pattern matches. Uses LRUCache (max size 32) for caching. newLlm(model: string) calls resolve and instantiates. Gemini and ApigeeLlm auto-registered at module load.

ApigeeLlm extends Gemini to integrate with Apigee API gateway as proxy for Gemini/Vertex AI models. Supports model name patterns matching /apigee\/.*/ with format: apigee/[<provider>/][<version>/]<model_id>. Constructor takes ApigeeLlmParams with additional proxyUrl field. apigeeToGeminiInitParams() determines vertexai mode by checking if model starts with 'apigee/vertex_ai/'. Overrides getHttpOptions() and getLiveHttpOptions() to set opts.baseUrl = this.proxyUrl, routing requests through Apigee. identifyApiVersion() extracts version from model string.

LlmRequest is interface representing request sent to LLM. It has fields: model (optional string, model name), contents (Content[] array of conversation messages), config (optional GenerateContentConfig), liveConnectConfig (LiveConnectConfig), toolsDict ({[key: string]: BaseTool} mapping tool names to instances, excluded from JSON serialization). appendInstructions() joins instructions with '\n\n' and appends to config.systemInstruction. appendTools() iterates tools, calls _getDeclaration() to get FunctionDeclaration, adds to toolsDict and config.tools. setOutputSchema() sets config.responseSchema and responseMimeType.

LlmResponse is interface representing response from LLM. It contains: content (optional Content, response content), groundingMetadata (optional GroundingMetadata), partial (optional boolean, unfinished stream), turnComplete (optional boolean), errorCode/errorMessage (optional, error info), interrupted (optional boolean), customMetadata (optional Record), usageMetadata (optional GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata), finishReason (optional FinishReason), liveSessionResumptionUpdate, inputTranscription, outputTranscription. createLlmResponse() converts GenerateContentResponse: if candidates exist with content, returns standard response; if no content, returns error response; if promptFeedback, returns error; else unknown error.

To register custom LLM implementation: 1) Create class extending BaseLlm, 2) Define static readonly supportedModels property (array of string literals or RegExp patterns), 3) Implement constructor with signature constructor({model}: {model: string}), 4) Implement abstract generateContentAsync(llmRequest: LlmRequest, stream?: boolean): AsyncGenerator<LlmResponse, void>, 5) Implement abstract connect(llmRequest: LlmRequest): Promise<BaseLlmConnection>, 6) Call LLMRegistry.register(YourCustomLlm). Pattern: class MyLlm extends BaseLlm { static override readonly supportedModels = [/my-model-.*/]; ... } LLMRegistry.register(MyLlm);

GoogleLLMVariant is enum with values: GEMINI_API (for using API Key) and VERTEX_AI (for using Vertex AI credentials). Variant determined by getGoogleLlmVariant() which checks GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI environment variable. The variant affects request preprocessing in Gemini.preprocessRequest(): for GEMINI_API variant, removes labels property (Google AI Studio doesn't support) and removes displayName from Blob/FileData objects (displayName is Vertex AI specific). For VERTEX_AI variant, fields preserved. apiBackend property determined from apiClient.vertexai.

The Session interface has structure: id (string, unique identifier), appName (string), userId (string), state (Record<string, unknown>), events (Event[] array), lastUpdateTime (number). Created via BaseSessionService.createSession(request: CreateSessionRequest) which takes appName, userId, state (optional), sessionId (optional, auto-generated). The createSession utility function fills defaults: userId defaults to '', state defaults to {}, events defaults to [], lastUpdateTime defaults to 0. Example implementation: InMemorySessionService generates session ID via randomUUID(), stores in nested map structure.

The State class maintains current value and pending delta with three prefixes: State.APP_PREFIX = 'app:' (application-wide state), State.USER_PREFIX = 'user:' (user-scoped state), State.TEMP_PREFIX = 'temp:' (temporary, excluded from persistence). Constructor takes value (current state Record) and delta (pending changes). Key methods: get<T>(key, defaultValue?) checks delta first then value; set(key, value) updates both; has(key) checks if key exists; hasDelta() returns true if delta has keys; update(delta) merges delta. Temp prefix exclusion happens in BaseSessionService.updateSessionState() which skips keys starting with State.TEMP_PREFIX.

BaseSessionService defines abstract methods: createSession(), getSession(), listSessions(), deleteSession(), appendEvent(). Non-abstract getOrCreateSession() tries getSession first, creates if not found. Base appendEvent() implementation: 1) Returns immediately if event.partial is true, 2) Calls updateSessionState() which iterates event.actions.stateDelta, skipping temp: prefixed keys, updates session.state, 3) Pushes event to session.events array, 4) Returns event. Subclasses like InMemorySessionService override appendEvent() to add lastUpdateTime updates and separate app:/user: prefixed state into dedicated storage.

InMemorySessionService implements in-memory session storage using nested Record objects: sessions (appName -> userId -> sessionId -> Session), userState (appName -> userId -> key -> value), appState (appName -> key -> value). GetSessionConfig options control event filtering: numRecentEvents (number) limits to last N events via slice(-config.numRecentEvents); afterTimestamp (number) filters events after timestamp by iterating backwards, finding last before, slicing from that point. getSession() returns cloneDeep() copy with filtering applied, then mergeState() merges app/user state back. listSessions() returns metadata without events/state.

The session service registry in core/src/sessions/registry.ts with getSessionServiceFromUri(uri: string): BaseSessionService. Currently supports only 'memory://' for in-memory sessions via isInMemoryConnectionString(uri) check. If matched, returns new InMemorySessionService(). For any other URI, throws Error('Unsupported session service URI: ${uri}'). Pattern mirrors artifact service registry which supports 'gs://bucket-name' for GCS and 'memory://' schemes.

The Runner passes stateDelta from user's request to session via createEventActions in runAsync lifecycle. After setting up session, if user provides stateDelta in params, creates user event with createEvent() that includes actions: stateDelta ? createEventActions({stateDelta}) : undefined. This user event appended to session via sessionService.appendEvent(). When appended, BaseSessionService.appendEvent() calls updateSessionState() which iterates stateDelta entries, skipping temp: prefixed keys, and updates session.state[key] = value. State accumulation works through iterative process: each event's stateDelta merged into session.state, subsequent events see accumulated state.
